title: Prophet Saleh and the She-Camel of Allah
summary: The story of Prophet Saleh 'alaihis salam, the people of Thamud, and the she-camel as a sign from Allah. (QS. Al-A'raf: 73-79; QS. Hud: 61-68; QS. Asy-Syu'ara: 141-159)
moral: Be thankful for Allah's blessings, obey His messenger, and do not harm His creatures. The arrogant and disobedient will bear the consequences.
pages: In a region called Al-Hijr lived the people of Thamud. They were skilled at carving rocky mountains into grand houses. Their life was prosperous, but they forgot to be thankful and worshipped others besides Allah.
Allah sent a messenger from among them, namely Prophet Saleh 'alaihis salam. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no god besides Him.' (QS. Al-A'raf: 73). But most of them refused.

They said, 'Give us a sign.' So Allah brought a she-camel as a sign of the truth. Scholars of tafsir mention that the camel came out of a large rock. Prophet Saleh said, 'This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign for you.'
Prophet Saleh also set a rule: the water in the well was shared, one day for the camel and one day for them. The camel drank calmly on its day, and everyone could get water.

'Let her eat on Allah's earth, and do not harm her, or you will be seized by a painful punishment,' warned Prophet Saleh (QS. Al-A'raf: 73). The camel walked calmly grazing in the field, living alongside them.
But some disobedient ones broke the rule. They harmed and killed the she-camel, though they had been warned. The camel was sad and grieved before that happened.

Prophet Saleh said, 'Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise that will not be belied.' (QS. Hud: 65). After that Allah destroyed the unjust ones, and Prophet Saleh and the believers were saved by Allah.

From this story we learn: to be thankful for Allah's blessings, to obey His messenger, not to be arrogant, and to love animals as Allah's creatures. Whoever follows the guidance will be saved. The end.
